turns.text: Can we buy the city e-bike battery packs from Brightcell Energy? They quote £104.00.
turns.reply:
Whether you can buy the city e-bike battery packs from Brightcell Energy depends on their onboarding status and certificates in Ledgerline. 

Here are the applicable rules:

1. **Food Contact / Battery Pack Qualification:**
   Battery packs touch food. Under the Purchase Policy, parts that come into contact with food "may be bought only from a supplier holding a **valid UN 38.3 certificate** on file in Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked **before the first order** is placed. An expired certificate counts as no certificate." (POL-PUR-001 §6.2; POL-SUP-003 §4.1).
   Furthermore, under Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy, "A UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if it was issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the order is placed." (AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1.1).

2. **Supplier Master Onboarding:**
   "A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed with them." (POL-PUR-001 §6.3).

3. **Pricing and Rate Contracts:**
   "Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the remarks." (POL-PUR-001 §7.2).

I cannot see or change Ledgerline ERP records, so I cannot check whether Brightcell Energy is set up as an active supplier, whether they have a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded, or whether £104.00 matches an approved rate contract. 

**Next steps:**
- Check Brightcell Energy in Ledgerline (`PUR-SUP-03`) to see if they are set up and active.
- Verify that a valid UN 38.3 certificate is on file for them meeting the 12-month issue and 60-day expiry requirements.
- Check whether an agreed rate contract exists covering the £104.00 quote.
